name: Glen's Bakehouse (Indiranagar)
why_it_matters: Started on 100 Feet Road in 2013 as a bakery-pizzeria hybrid; now sixteen-plus outlets across south India. The red velvet, tiramisu and wood-fired pizzas are the trio that built the brand.
insider_tip: Friday and Saturday night the queue runs an hour for desserts — go between 4pm and 6pm for fresh-out-of-the-oven slices and a free table. The bakehouse loaf is the locals' takeaway pick.
signature_address: 1027, 100 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: Glen's Bakehouse (Lavelle Road)
why_it_matters: Founder Glen Williams (also of Sweet Chariot and Toit) opened the original on 100 Feet Road in 2013, then took over the old Java City spot on Lavelle Road in 2016. A live bakery and a hot kitchen under one roof — the closest Bengaluru gets to a European bakehouse-with-a-pub-feel.
insider_tip: The weekend roast is a sleeper hit — call ahead because portions sell out by 2pm. Sit upstairs at the Lavelle Road outlet for the quieter side of the room.
signature_address: 24/1, Lavelle Road, Richmond Town, Bengaluru 560001

name: Hotel Janatha (Malleshwaram)
why_it_matters: A 1965 darshini on the same Sajjan Rao Circle stretch as the VV Puram food street, Janatha is one of two Basavanagudi names tied to the khali dosa — a soft, plain dosa eaten with coconut chutney. Workhorse menu, low prices, full at 8 am sharp.
insider_tip: Two sittings only — 6.30 am to noon and 3 pm to 7 pm. Order khali dosa with extra chutney; the masala version is solid but the plain one is what people return for.
signature_address: 26, Diagonal Road, Sajjan Rao Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Hotel Janatha (VV Puram)
why_it_matters: Old-school Malleshwaram tiffin room — thin, glistening Mysore masala dosa with a fierce red chutney lining and a filter coffee that locals rate above several flashier rivals. Tile-floor, vintage-board, walk-in-only kind of place.
insider_tip: Tuesday is Lord Hanuman day in this neighbourhood — Janatha gets slammed pre-temple. Aim for 8am or 11am off-peak. Order uddina vada with the dosa for the full Karnataka tiffin set.
signature_address: 27, 8th Cross Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru 560003

name: Truffles (Indiranagar)
why_it_matters: Bengaluru's burger institution since 2004 — the chain that taught a generation of techies what a thick double-patty looks like. The Indiranagar outlet is the busiest in the group and the queue is part of the ritual.
insider_tip: Put your name on the host list and walk over to Toit or Glen's for an hour — they will SMS when your table is ready. Late lunch (3pm-4:30pm) is the only quiet window.
signature_address: Ground Floor, K.P. Square, 307, 100 Feet Road, Binnamangala, Stage 1, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms (MTR)
why_it_matters: Founded in 1924 by the Maiya brothers from Parampalli, MTR invented rava idli during WWII rice shortages and remains the city's most cited Udupi institution. The Lalbagh Road original is also one of only ~150 entries on the World's Legendary Restaurants list.
insider_tip: Take a token from the counter on entry, then wait upstairs for table service; the lunch thali (1 to 3 pm) is unlimited and the better-value meal vs. a dosa rush. Closed Mondays.
signature_address: 14, Lalbagh Road, Mavalli, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560027

name: Vidyarthi Bhavan
why_it_matters: Started in 1943 as a tiny eatery for students of nearby colleges, Vidyarthi Bhavan's slow-cooked, ghee-soaked masala dosa is the benchmark Bengaluru measures all others against. The narrow Gandhi Bazaar shopfront and shared-table format have not changed in eight decades.
insider_tip: Arrive between 7 and 9 am on a weekday; the queue snakes around the lane after 10 am and wait times can hit 45 minutes. Closed Mondays. Cash and UPI only.
signature_address: 32, Gandhi Bazaar Main Road, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: CTR Shri Sagar (Central Tiffin Room)
why_it_matters: Established in 1920 by Y.V. Subramanyam, CTR is the city's reference point for benne (butter) masala dosa — crisp outer, soft inner, served with a thick coconut chutney. Now formally called Shri Sagar but locals still queue for what they grew up calling CTR.
insider_tip: The kitchen shuts between 12.30 pm and 4 pm — plan a breakfast or evening visit, not lunch. Pair the benne dosa with khara bath rather than a second dosa for the fuller flavour spread.
signature_address: 152, 7th Cross Road, Margosa Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

name: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
why_it_matters: Opened in 1965 by K.V. Nagesh Rao and K.N. Saraswati, Brahmin's serves only four things — idli, vada, khara bath, kesari bath — and is regularly named the city's best plate of soft idli with watery, mint-tinted coconut chutney. The same family runs it three generations on.
insider_tip: Stand-and-eat only, no chairs. Get there before 8.30 am to skip the office queue, and ask for the chutney refill — they pour generously if you don't waste the first cup. Closed Sundays.
signature_address: Ranga Rao Road, Near Shankar Mutt, Shankarapuram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Airlines Hotel
area: Madras Bank Road, off Lavelle Road
why_it_matters: The city's first drive-in restaurant, opened 1968 by Kalarickal Thomas and S.N. Rao. A century-old banyan shades the open-air tables and the kitchen pours close to 1,000 cups of filter coffee a day, mostly to office regulars who park up and stay an hour.
insider_tip: Eat in the garden, not the indoor section. Mornings 7-10am are the cleanest hour for coffee; the dosa batter peaks at breakfast.
signature_address: 4 Madras Bank Road, off Lavelle Road, Bengaluru 560001

name: Veena Stores
why_it_matters: A standing-only counter on 15th Cross since 1977, Veena Stores is the place locals send first-timers when they want to argue that Malleshwaram has the city's softest idli. The chutney spread (coconut, mint, peanut) is unusually generous for a street counter.
insider_tip: Open all seven days, 7 am to noon and 4 pm onwards. Ask for an extra chutney pour at the counter — they'll oblige if you don't push. UPI works; carry small notes for the tip.
signature_address: 187, 15th Cross, Margosa Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

name: New Modern Hotel
why_it_matters: Opened 1959 near Minerva Circle, NMH was a gathering room for Kannada writers (DVG, H.V. Seetharamaiah) and theatre figures (Girish Kasaravalli) — its masala dosa and rich badam halwa are both Basavanagudi reference dishes. Lodging-and-boarding format from a different era.
insider_tip: Be in by 9 am to avoid the office rush. Order the masala dosa with a side of badam halwa — sweet first or last is a long-running local debate worth settling for yourself.
signature_address: 143, Dr. A.N. Krishna Rao Road, Near Minerva Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Hotel Dwaraka
why_it_matters: Started 1972 on Bull Temple Road and now in NR Colony, Hotel Dwaraka is widely credited as the originator of Bengaluru's kali dosa — a soft, oil-less dosa cooked on a closed pan that arrived to the city before any other restaurant put it on a menu. Cash-only, self-service.
insider_tip: Cash only, no card or wallet. Avarekalu khara bath is seasonal (Dec to Feb when local field beans are in) — ask before ordering, it's the better khara bath outside the season.
signature_address: 7th Cross, NR Colony, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560004

name: Vasudev Adiga's
why_it_matters: K.N. Vasudev Adiga, son of Brahmin's Coffee Bar founder K.V. Nageshwar Adiga, opened the first Adiga's on DVG Road in 1993 as a clean, low-priced darshini. The chain is now the city's reference quality bar for what a darshini should taste like — same recipes across 12+ Bengaluru outlets.
insider_tip: The Jayanagar 4th Block branch runs a faster turnaround than the AC restaurants — pay first at the counter, then collect from the kitchen window. Best for a 15-minute weekday breakfast stop.
signature_address: 39th Cross, 4th Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560011

name: The Fatty Bao
why_it_matters: Olive Bar and Kitchen's pan-Asian gastrobar — the Indiranagar rooftop where Bengaluru learnt to take steamed bao seriously. Chocolate dim sum dessert is now copied across India.
insider_tip: Sit on the open terrace for the after-work crowd; the indoor bar gets loud after 9pm. The bao platter plus a single khow suey feeds two comfortably without ordering mains.
signature_address: 610, 3rd Floor, 12th Main Road, Off 80 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560008

name: The Permit Room
why_it_matters: Indian gastropub that pulls food from five southern states — Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra, Telangana and Tamil Nadu — and pairs them with filter-coffee cocktails and tap beer. The format that nudged Bengaluru's bar food past kebabs.
insider_tip: Order the kerala parotta with beef ularthiyathu plus one filter-coffee old fashioned — that's the signature combo. Tuesday and Wednesday are calmest; weekends need a 7pm or earlier slot.
signature_address: 55, Lower Palace Orchards, 100 Feet Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: Third Wave Coffee Roasters
why_it_matters: Bengaluru's homegrown answer to global third-wave coffee — co-founders Anirudh Sharma, Ayush Bathwal and Sushant Goel set up the first specialty cafe-roastery of its kind in the country in Koramangala, then scaled to 100+ outlets. The Indiranagar room is where the brand still feels closest to its roastery roots.
insider_tip: Order the single-estate pour over of the week — the barista will quote the farm and altitude unprompted. Skip the flavoured lattes; the milk-and-bean ratios are tuned for the flat white and cortado.
signature_address: Ground Floor, 80 30th Feet Main Road, CMH Road, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: The Hole in the Wall Cafe
why_it_matters: Started in 2009 by Bangalore couple Lynn Dcosta and Nathan Harris in a no-frills garage — became the city's de facto Sunday brunch institution. Continental breakfast done honestly, affordably, and the same way for 17 years. Mondays closed, weekend queues cheerful.
insider_tip: No reservations — show up before 9am on Saturday or after 11.30am Sunday to skip the worst of the wait. Closed Mondays. The all-day breakfast is the move; the dinner menu is forgettable.
signature_address: 8th Main Road, Koramangala 4th Block, Bengaluru 560034

name: Dyu Art Cafe
signature_dish: filter coffee with the day's sandwich
why_it_matters: A restored Kerala-style heritage home with open courtyard, oxide flooring and gabled roof — the rotating gallery wall has hung work by city-based and visiting artists for over a decade. Set the tone for Koramangala's cafe culture before the area went mainstream.
insider_tip: Sit in the courtyard, not the upstairs gallery — the light is better and you can hear the bird call from the mango tree. Closed early evenings some weekdays; check before driving across town.
signature_address: 23/22, 1st Cross Road, KHB MIG Colony, Koramangala 8th Block, Bengaluru 560095

name: Mahesh Lunch Home
must_try: neer dosa with chicken ghee roast
why_it_matters: Bengaluru outpost of S.C. Karkera's Mangalorean institution founded in Mumbai in 1977. The chef-brings-the-tray-of-fish ritual and butter garlic mussels remain unchanged across forty-plus years.
insider_tip: Lunchtime thali with surmai, bangda and a neer dosa is the cheapest way in; a la carte at dinner runs nearly double. Pick your fish from the chef's tray before ordering — that's how regulars get the freshest catch.
signature_address: 2011, 1st Floor, 100 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: Halli Mane
why_it_matters: Halli Mane (Kannada for 'village home') is the city's most cited address for rural Karnataka vegetarian cooking — ragi mudde, akki rotti, jolada rotti, bisi bele bath, obbattu — served on banana leaves in a low-seating, village-themed room. Operating on Sampige Road for 20+ years.
insider_tip: The unlimited weekend breakfast buffet is the best value way to taste eight to ten Karnataka village dishes in one sitting. Ask the server which obbattu (holige) filling is freshest that day — coconut, dal or jaggery.
signature_address: 14, 3rd Cross, Sampige Road, Malleshwaram, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560003

name: Toit Brewpub
why_it_matters: Founded in 2010 by Sibi Venkataraju, Arun George and Mukesh Tolani, Toit is the brewpub that put Bengaluru on India's craft beer map. The three-floor 100 Feet Road flagship still pulls weekend queues for the Toit Weiss and Tintin Toit on tap.
insider_tip: Walk in before 6:30pm on a weekday for the rooftop and you'll skip the 90-minute wait that builds after 7pm. The Toit Weiss is the safer first pour than the rotating seasonals.
signature_address: 298, 100 Feet Road, Binnamangala, Stage 1, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: Karavalli
why_it_matters: Open since 1990 inside what is now Vivanta Bengaluru Residency Road, Karavalli is India's longest-running fine-dining south-west-coast restaurant. The tamarind-tree garden room and chef Naren Thimmaiah's recipes are the textbook reference for Mangalorean, Coorgi and Kerala-coast cooking.
insider_tip: Reserve the open verandah seating, not the indoor wood-panel room — the garden is the experience. Ask the captain for the off-menu daily catch from the crab and karimeen tray.
signature_address: Vivanta Bengaluru Residency Road, 41/3 Mahatma Gandhi Road, Bengaluru 560025

name: Smoke House Deli
why_it_matters: Riyaaz Amlani's Impresario all-day deli, born 2009 — the format that gave Indian metros their first credible take on smoked meats, hand-drawn-mural cafes and brunch-as-a-routine. Indiranagar branch is the city's go-to brunch booking.
insider_tip: Sunday brunch packs the room from noon — book the corner banquette near the bar for the calmest seating. The english breakfast plus a smoked chicken sandwich split between two is the value play.
signature_address: Ward 72, Plot 1209, 100 Feet Road, HAL 2nd Stage, Doopanahalli, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: Meghana Foods
why_it_matters: The Andhra biryani most copied in Bengaluru — operating since 2006, the Koramangala 5th Block flagship is the city's go-to for spice-heavy chicken and mutton biryani. Queues form even on weekday evenings.
insider_tip: Token system: collect a token at the entrance, then loop back when called rather than standing in line. Order extra raita and salan — both are part of the biryani's character. Skip dinner peak (8-10pm) for 30+ minute waits.
signature_address: 124, 1st A Cross Road, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru 560095

name: Nagarjuna
must_try: andhra veg meal on banana leaf
why_it_matters: Founded 1984 by N. Krishna Reddy as the original outlet, this Residency Road branch is the template every Andhra meals chain in the city imitates. Unlimited rice, ghee and ten-plus accompaniments served on a banana leaf.
insider_tip: Lunch (12-3pm) is when the meals are freshest — by dinner the spread thins. Outlets in Koramangala and Indiranagar follow the same recipe, but the Residency Road original still pulls regulars after four decades.
signature_address: 44/1, Residency Road, near Mayo Hall, Shanthala Nagar, Bengaluru 560025

name: Le Cirque Signature
why_it_matters: Indian outpost of the Manhattan institution founded by Sirio Maccioni in 1974, opened at The Leela Palace in 2014. The only Franco-Italian fine-dining room of this pedigree in south India — wine list runs to 250+ labels and the imported French cheese trolley is the city's largest.
insider_tip: Dinner-only — open 6:30pm to 11:30pm. Skip the à la carte and book the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing; it works out cheaper than ordering three courses solo.
signature_address: The Leela Palace Bengaluru, 23 HAL Old Airport Road, Kodihalli, Bengaluru 560008

name: The Royal Afghan
why_it_matters: Poolside open-air kebab institution at ITC Windsor since the hotel opened in 1982 — the same menu for over four decades. The dal bukhara has simmered for 24 hours every day for 40+ years, and the kakori is still minced and skewered to the original ITC recipe that put north-west frontier cuisine on India's hotel-restaurant map.
insider_tip: Book a poolside table after sunset — the open-flame tandoor sits in plain sight and the smoke hits differently outdoors. Lunch is rarely full; dinner needs a week's notice on weekends.
signature_address: ITC Windsor, 25 Windsor Square, Golf Course Road, Bengaluru 560052

name: Toscano
must_try: goat cheese rucola and pear salad with parmaham
why_it_matters: Founded by Chefs Jean Michel Jasserand and Goutham Balasubramanian, the UB City flagship is Bengaluru's longest-running Italian fine-dining room. Times Food Award 'Best Italian Restaurant in Bangalore' multiple years; the pasta is rolled in-house daily and the wine list is the deepest Italian-only selection in the city.
insider_tip: Sit on the outdoor terrace facing Vittal Mallya Road — the only UB City restaurant with proper alfresco seating. The four-course set lunch on weekdays is the value play.
signature_address: Level 3, UB City Mall, 24 Vittal Mallya Road, Bengaluru 560001

name: Koshy's
why_it_matters: P.O. Koshy opened the bakery in 1940 and the Parade Cafe followed on St Mark's Road in 1952; Nehru, Khrushchev, Marshal Tito and Queen Elizabeth II were all catered to here. Three generations on, the wood-panelled hall still pulls journalists, lawyers and old Bangaloreans for breakfast and beer.
insider_tip: Open 9am-11.30pm. The bar (Jewel Box) on the side is the writers' corner; the main hall is breakfast country. Cash and UPI both work.
signature_address: 39 St Mark's Road, Shanthala Nagar, Bengaluru 560001

name: Empire Restaurant
why_it_matters: Abdul Rahim Haji took over a Central Street eatery in 1966 and renamed it after MG Road's old Empire Theatre; the late-1980s 'coin parotta' — a leftover-dough accident — became the cult dish. From this Mosque Road kitchen the family has grown a 45-outlet, ₹560 crore Bengaluru chain.
insider_tip: Open till 4am — the post-pub biryani run is the local move. The Mosque Road outlet is the original; queues from 9pm.
signature_address: 34 Mosque Road, Frazer Town, Bengaluru 560005

name: Maverick & Farmer Coffee
why_it_matters: Founded in 2018 by Sreeram G, Tej Thammaiah and Ashish D'abreo — one of India's few bean-to-cup roasters that grow on their own Coorg estate. The lab-style menu (cold-smoked coffee, clarified cappuccino, fermented experiments) put Bengaluru's specialty scene on the global map.
insider_tip: Ask for the cupping flight if it's running — the barista will walk you through three estates side by side. The clarified cappuccino is the conversation starter; the cherry soda is the surprise.
signature_address: 118, 5th B Cross Road, Koramangala 4th Block, Bengaluru 560034

name: Truffles (Koramangala)
why_it_matters: The benchmark Bengaluru burger — generous patties, fries and milkshakes that built the city's casual-burger template before the global chains arrived. Now eight dine-in outlets, with the Koramangala 5th Block branch the busiest after St. Marks Road.
insider_tip: Weekend evening waits hit 60-90 minutes; go weekday lunch 12:30-1:30 or late afternoon 4-6 to walk in. The Koramangala outlet is closer to the original feel than the newer Indiranagar 100 Feet Road branch.
signature_address: 28, 4th B Cross Road, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru 560095

name: Windmills Craftworks
why_it_matters: Opened 2012 in Whitefield as India's first integrated jazz theatre and microbrewery, with a curated design library on the same floor. Wednesday-Saturday evenings host live jazz, blues and fusion acts that tech-park regulars build dinners around.
insider_tip: Reserve the jazz theatre side (separate from the bar) for the live-music nights — bar-side seats hear the music but miss the room. Cover charges apply on headliner nights; check the calendar before booking.
signature_address: 6th Floor, 331, Road 5B, EPIP Zone, Whitefield, Bengaluru 560066

name: Chianti Ristorante & Wine Bar
why_it_matters: Koramangala's long-running Italian — first opened here over a decade ago, now seven outlets across the city. The original 5th Block flagship still sets the bar for honest pasta and wood-fired pizza without fine-dining theatre.
insider_tip: Lunch sets are the value play: two courses for under ₹1000 weekdays. Reserve a window booth on the upper level; ground-floor tables are louder once the bar fills up after 8pm.
signature_address: 12, 80 Feet Road, 5th Block, Koramangala, Bengaluru 560095

name: Anand Sweets & Savouries
why_it_matters: Founded 1988 by Anand Dadu — Bengaluru's market-leading premium mithai chain. 15 city stores, airport retail at 15 Indian airports, and a flagship in Jayanagar that's the default sweet-box for weddings and Diwali across Karnataka.
insider_tip: Order at the takeaway counter for sweet-boxes; the small dine-in serves chaat and chole bhature for the wait. Festival season (Diwali, Sankranti) — order kesar badam barfi 2 days ahead.
signature_address: Shop 4 & 5, D No 14/39, 27th Cross, 4th Block, Jayanagar, Bengaluru 560041

name: Taaza Thindi
why_it_matters: Self-service breakfast counter run by the Mayura Group (founded 1976) — fluffy rava idli, ghee-soaked khara bath and a 4.9 Zomato rating that locals defend like a local stock. One of the cleanest, fastest South-Indian tiffin counters in the city.
insider_tip: Open 7am-12pm and 4pm-9:30pm; rava idli batch is hottest before 9am. Pay at the cashier first, then take the chit to the counter. UPI works.
signature_address: 1004, Ground Floor, Next to HDFC Bank, 26th Main Road, Jayanagar 4th T Block, Bengaluru 560041

name: Hari Super Sandwich
why_it_matters: Bengaluru's most famous sandwich counter — a tiny pure-veg shop on VV Puram Food Street that fills you up under ₹100 with sandwiches and chaat the city has crowned a street-food institution.
insider_tip: Crowds peak 7pm-10pm — go right at 5pm opening for the freshest bread. The chocolate sandwich sounds like a stunt; it is a stunt that works. Standing-only, eat on the street.
signature_address: 2, National High School Road, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru 560004

name: Burma Burma
why_it_matters: All-vegetarian Burmese — khow suey, tea-leaf salad and samuza hincho (samosa-in-broth) that introduced Bengaluru to a cuisine it had no template for. Three city outlets (Indiranagar, Brigade Road, Yelahanka) and a no-alcohol policy that keeps it food-first.
insider_tip: No reservations — first-come-first-served. Arrive 6:30pm sharp for dinner or face a 45-minute wait. The dedicated tea menu is genuinely good; try a Burmese milk tea flight alongside the khow suey rather than defaulting to soft drinks.
signature_address: 607, 12th Main Road, 7th Cross, HAL 2nd Stage, Indiranagar, Bengaluru 560038

name: The Rameshwaram Cafe
why_it_matters: The viral 2023-2024 South Indian quick-service phenomenon — ghee podi idli and benne masala dosa served counter-style at sub-₹100 price points. The Brookefield outlet reopened on 8 March 2024 after the on-premise blast and remains operational with the same crowds it had before.
insider_tip: Breakfast (7-10am) is when the idlis and dosas are freshest and the wait is shortest. By 11am queues stretch outside. Order at the counter, collect from the next station — the system rewards arriving solo or in pairs over big groups.
signature_address: Plot No. 1, Green Avenue, ITPL Main Road, Brookefield, Bengaluru 560037

name: Jamavar
why_it_matters: The Leela Palace's flagship Indian room, named after the Kashmiri brocade and built around a regional survey of dum-cooked north and south Indian classics. Awarded by La Liste in both 2025 (82.5) and 2026 (80) — one of the few Karnataka restaurants on that global list. Chef Sahadevan handles south Indian, Chef Jasbir runs the north Indian section.
insider_tip: Request a garden-terrace table for dinner and pre-order the raan — it needs 24 hours to braise. The vegetarian dum biryani is the quiet hero non-veg diners regret missing.
signature_address: The Leela Palace Bengaluru, 23 HAL Old Airport Road, Kodihalli, Bengaluru 560008

name: Yauatcha
why_it_matters: Hakkasan Group's Bengaluru dim sum house — same kitchen lineage as the Michelin-starred London original. The all-day dim sum tea-house format runs 40+ steamed, baked and fried varieties plus a French-trained patisserie counter; opened at 1 MG in 2014 and still the city's gold standard for Cantonese fine dining.
insider_tip: Dim sum lunch is half the dinner price for the same kitchen and skill. The vegetarian dim sum platter is one of India's best — the truffle edamame dumpling alone justifies the trip.
signature_address: Level 5, 1 MG Lido Mall, MG Road, Bengaluru 560001

name: Indian Coffee House
why_it_matters: The Bengaluru cooperative was formed in 1957, the original MG Road branch ran from 1959 until April 2009, and the Workers' Cooperative reopened it on Church Street the same year — same turbaned waiters, same red-and-white interior, same prices that haven't moved with the city.
insider_tip: Behind Shringar Shopping Complex on Church Street. The cutlets are made fresh after 4pm; mornings are coffee-and-paper crowd.
signature_address: G-37 & 38, Indian Coffee House, Ground Floor, behind Shringar Shopping Complex, Church Street, Bengaluru 560001

name: Albert Bakery
why_it_matters: Mohammed Suleman opened it in 1902 and named it after Prince Albert to court Frazer Town's Anglo clientele; the great-grandson Sabir runs it today. During Ramzan the queue for bheja (goat brain) puffs and mutton samosas wraps around Mosque Road every evening.
insider_tip: Opens 3pm, closes by 7-8pm — go before 5pm or join the queue. Cash easier than card. During Ramzan the food street outside is the bigger experience.
signature_address: 172 Mosque Road, Frazer Town, Bengaluru 560005

name: The Only Place
why_it_matters: Haroon Sait opened it in 1965 to feed the Peace Corps Americans and Iranian guests staying at his family's hotel — a Japanese diner suggested the name because it was the only place serving steaks and apple pie in the city. The 40-year-old apple pie recipe and the steaks are both unchanged.
insider_tip: Now on Museum Road in a 150-seater with park-bench seating; the older Brigade Road outpost has shut. The al fresco section is the one to ask for.
signature_address: 13 Museum Road, Richmond Town, Bengaluru 560025

name: Imperial Restaurant
why_it_matters: Running since 1954, Imperial is one of the city's two surviving vintage Mughlai chains — Cunningham Road is the original. The biryani-and-fried-chicken-kebab combo is a Bangalore late-night ritual and the kitchen stays open until 1am.
insider_tip: Open till 1am — many regulars come post-cinema. Original outlet is on Cunningham; the Residency Road and Indiranagar branches are newer.
signature_address: 20 Cunningham Road, Vasanth Nagar, Bengaluru 560052

name: VB Bakery
why_it_matters: Visvesvarapuram Brahmin Bakery — landmark Iyengar bakery at the entrance of VV Puram Food Street, 65+ years old. Many credit it with seeding the Iyengar-bakery template now copied across south Bengaluru.
insider_tip: Get here before 7pm — the khara bun ("KBC") with spicy peanut filling sells out by mid-evening. Pair with a Mangalore bun next door. Cash and UPI both work.
signature_address: 1, Sajjan Rao Circle, VV Puram, Basavanagudi, Bengaluru 560004

name: Bhagatram Sweets
why_it_matters: Started 1948 by Bhagatram, a Sindhi migrant who landed in Bengaluru via Delhi, Mumbai and Chennai. The Commercial Street counter feeds ~4,000 people a day and is the city's reference for North Indian-style mithai and chole bhature.
insider_tip: Saturday afternoons and festival eves are pure scrum — go weekday 11am or 4pm. Stand at the chaat counter for the dahi vada, then queue separately at the sweets counter. UPI works; cash for fastest service.
signature_address: 10, Commercial Street, Shivajinagar, Bengaluru 560001

name: Lavonne Cafe
why_it_matters: Started in 2012 by pastry chefs Vinesh Johny, Avin Thaliath and Lijo Chandy as the country's first international baking and pastry arts academy with a cafe attached — every dessert leaving the counter is school-grade. This is the dessert benchmark every other Bengaluru patisserie is measured against.
insider_tip: The custom cake counter takes 48-hour notice for the entremets — worth it for a birthday. Walk-in for the tartes and croissants midweek; weekend mall traffic kills the experience.
signature_address: Lower Ground Floor, Forum Shantiniketan Mall, ITPL Main Road, Whitefield, Bengaluru 560048
